# "The student is the most important person and the city is the main challenge for the university."

**Salvador Alva, rector of Tecnológico de Monterrey until 2020, visited EAFIT and highlighted the collaboration between the two universities as benchmarks for influence and leadership in solving problems in Mexico and Colombia. He shared some key phrases that reflect the future of education, humanism, and the role of these types of organizations globally.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- [Publications](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/publicaciones)
- [The EAFIT student](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/publicaciones/el-eafitense)
- [Edition 121](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/publicaciones/el-eafitense/edicion-121)
- "The student is the most important person and the city is the main challenge for the university."

###### Video

![](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/ee60sg0aU00/maxresdefault.jpg)

> **We must prepare young people; they are the ones who will transform society, who will address problems, and those problems are opportunities. Today, entrepreneurship is the engine of the economy, and EAFIT must be the university of entrepreneurship, training these leaders with a different, humanistic mindset, because that is the only thing that will change society.**

> **For years we built a world with borders, and today communication is breaking them down. We are preparing for human beings to reach their full potential, to contribute to society, with cities acting as magnets for talent. Transformations are taking place in universities, starting in cities.**

> **The university must be connected to real-life challenges. That's why we decided to change the entire model towards learning challenges, where the challenge is a real-life situation, linked to a company, that lends itself to students facing it.**

> **The university needs to learn to let go, to collectively decide what it will abandon; to choose two or three projects that will transform it, and those are the ones to which resources should be allocated. Don't overload yourselves with programs! Being irrelevant is the easiest thing to do. The university must stop thinking only about Medellín; it must consider Medellín's role on the planet and become relevant.**

###### Viruses versus bacteria: PhageLife's proposal for the swine sector from EAFIT

On a pig farm, a bacterial infection can jeopardize the animals' health and the farm's productivity. Furthermore, the problem becomes more complex when the bacteria stop responding to the antibiotics that previously combated them. To explore another approach, the company [PhageLife](https://phagelife.co/) is developing customized solutions using bacteriophages, naturally occurring viruses capable of eliminating specific bacteria.
